_comment: Hand-written items for topics the extractor cannot serve. In this source those are tables whose row meaning lives in arrow glyphs with no Unicode mapping, so the text layer holds only the bare figure. Each entry is transcribed from the page image named in sourceNote; a topic listed here replaces the extractor's output for that topic. Verify against the figure in the reader before trusting a number.

general-vmc.sourceNote: Transcribed from public/source/reference-v7-1/page-18.webp. Arrow glyphs in the source denote direction: horizontal from cloud, vertical from cloud, above, below.

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class G and Class E: flight visibility?
items.answer: 5000 m; 8 km above 10,000 ft

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class G and Class E: distance from cloud?
items.answer: 1500 m horizontally, 1000 ft vertically

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class G: when may you instead remain clear of cloud and in sight of ground or water?
items.answer: When below 3000 ft AMSL or 1000 ft AGL, whichever is higher, provided radio is carried and used on the appropriate frequency.

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class D: flight visibility?
Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class D: distance from cloud?
items.answer: 600 m horizontally, 1000 ft above, 500 ft below

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class C: flight visibility?
items.answer: 5000 m; 8 km above 10,000 ft

items.prompt: Visual Meteorological Conditions — Class C: distance from cloud?
items.answer: 1500 m horizontally, 1000 ft vertically

approach-speeds.sourceNote: Transcribed from public/source/reference-v7-1/page-48.webp, AIP ENR 1.5 Para 1.15 Handling Speeds. Speeds in knots. The bracketed figure is the max speed for reversal procedures.

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category A: VAT, and max speeds for circling and missed approach?
items.answer: VAT below 91; circling 100; missed approach 110

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category B: VAT, and max speeds for circling and missed approach?
items.answer: VAT 91–120; circling 135; missed approach 150

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category C: VAT, and max speeds for circling and missed approach?
items.answer: VAT 121–140; circling 180; missed approach 240

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category D: VAT, and max speeds for circling and missed approach?
items.answer: VAT 141–165; circling 205; missed approach 265

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category E: VAT, and max speeds for circling and missed approach?
items.answer: VAT 166–210; circling 240; missed approach 275

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category A: initial/intermediate and final approach speed ranges?
items.answer: Initial and intermediate 90–150 (110 max for reversal procedures); final 70–100

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category B: initial/intermediate and final approach speed ranges?
items.answer: Initial and intermediate 120–180 (140 max for reversal procedures); final 85–130

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — Category C: initial/intermediate and final approach speed ranges?
items.answer: Initial and intermediate 160–240; final 115–160

items.prompt: Approach Speeds — helicopters: speeds?
items.answer: Initial and intermediate 70–120; final 60–90; missed approach 90. No VAT and no circling speed.

approach-test-tolerances.sourceNote: Transcribed from public/source/reference-v7-1/page-48.webp, Part 61 MOS Volume 4, Schedule 8, Section 1, Table 5.

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — 2D approach lateral path tracking, using azimuth guidance?
items.answer: Within ± 5° of nominated track

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — 2D approach lateral path tracking, using a lateral course deviation indicator?
items.answer: Within ± ½ scale deflection of nominated track

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — 2D approach tracking on a DME or GNSS arc?
items.answer: Within ± 2 NM of the arc

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — 3D approach vertical path?
items.answer: ± ½ scale deflection, or ± 75 ft for an RNP BARO VNAV procedure

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — minimum altitude?
items.answer: +100 ft, −0 ft at the published minima descent altitude; the missed approach must not be initiated below decision altitude.

items.prompt: Instrument Approach Tolerances (flight test) — 3D approach lateral path tracking?
items.answer: As for 2D, according to the lateral path guidance being used.

approach-procedure-turns.sourceNote: Transcribed from the reversal procedures diagram on public/source/reference-v7-1/page-47.webp, AIP ENR 1.5 Para 2.8. Timings are the diagram's own labels.

items.prompt: Reversal Procedures — a 45°/180° procedure turn: outbound timing, and the 45° leg?
items.answer: Outbound 1 to 3 minutes, then the 45° leg for 1 minute (Cat A and B) or 1 minute 15 seconds (Cat C and D), before the 180° turn.

items.prompt: Reversal Procedures — an 80°/260° procedure turn: outbound timing?
items.answer: 1 to 3 minutes.

items.prompt: Reversal Procedures — base turns: what outbound legs are published?
items.answer: 1, 2 or 3 minutes, or the published DME distance.

items.prompt: Reversal Procedures — name the three types.
items.answer: 45°/180° procedure turn; 80°/260° procedure turn; base turn

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — what is VMCA, and which radial marks it?
items.answer: Minimum control speed, air — the red radial. The minimum speed at which it is possible to maintain directional control of the aircraft with the critical engine inoperative.

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — on what conditions is VMCA determined?
items.answer: Critical engine inoperative; live engine at take-off power; landing gear retracted; a maximum of 5 degrees bank towards the live engine; propeller feathered (only for aircraft with automatic feathering devices)

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — what is VMCG?
items.answer: Minimum control speed, ground. The minimum speed, whilst on the ground, at which it is possible to maintain direction using only aerodynamic controls — critical engine inoperative, live engine at take-off power.

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — what is VSSE, and what is it for?
items.answer: Single engine safety speed: the speed below which intentional simulated engine failures should not be conducted. A manufacturer-stated speed intended to provide a margin above VMCA.

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — what is VYSE, and which radial marks it?
items.answer: Single engine best rate of climb speed — the blue radial. The speed at which the best rate of climb can be achieved with the critical engine inoperative.

items.prompt: Speed Definitions — on what conditions is VYSE determined?
items.answer: Critical engine inoperative; live engine at take-off power; landing gear retracted

approach-types.sourceNote: Transcribed from public/source/reference-v7-1/page-41.webp, Part 61 MOS Volume 2, Schedule 2, Section 5.

items.prompt: Types of Instrument Approaches — which are 2D?
items.answer: NDB; VOR; DME or GNSS arrival procedure; RNP APCH LNAV and RNP APCH LP (previously RNAV GNSS); LLZ

items.prompt: Types of Instrument Approaches — which are 3D?
items.answer: ILS; MLS; GLS; RNP-LNAV/VNAV (Baro); RNP-LPV

items.prompt: Types of Instrument Approaches — which are azimuth guidance operations?
items.answer: NDB; DME or GNSS arrival procedure using an ADF

items.prompt: Types of Instrument Approaches — which are course deviation indicator operations?
items.answer: ILS; LLZ; RNP APCH LNAV and RNP APCH LP; RNP-LNAV/VNAV (Baro); RNP-LPV; VOR; DME/GNSS arrival procedure using a CDI
